label: sprites/fw_steam.spr: a steam puff that rises and thins, animated

againstClass.words: starts too bright: an attack in its envelope
does not end dark: a decay in its envelope

R1.reason: The picture is a flat, light-grey disc with a hard edge, on a near-black ground. It has no billowing, no soft falloff and no vapour texture, so it does not read as a steam puff. It is a plain disc.

R2.reason: One 32 x 32 frame, with the disc filling most of it and an empty border (border measure 0, which is fine). The size suits a puff, but the effect does not fill the frame as a puff would: it is a hard-edged shape, not a cloud that spreads.

R3.reason: Uniform neutral light grey. It is plausible for an additive steam puff, but it is a flat fill with no tonal variation, and no class colour is measured to compare against. Not clearly off, but not steam-like either.

R4.reason: The sprite has one frame, so there is no rise, no thinning and no growth. The envelope measures fail on all three counts: the peak is at frame 0 (class 0.2 to 0.6), it starts at full brightness (first 1, class 0 to 0.35), and it does not end dark (last 1, class 0 to 0.1). The brief asks for an animated puff, and this is a still.

R5.reason: A valid GoldSrc sprite: type parallel, format additive, 32 x 32, one frame, named fw_steam to match sprites/fw_steam.spr. The file reads back with these values, and additive is a sensible format for steam.
